blocks.text: BACOLOD CITY, NEGROS OCCIDENTAL, Philippines — Roadworthy traditional public utility vehicles (PUVs) should be allowed to continue operating despite the implementation of the Public Transport Modernization Program, Deputy House Speaker and Bacolod Rep. Alfredo Abelardo Benitez said here recently, backing transport groups’ call for a status quo. During a meeting with local transport groups on Nov. 20, Benitez assured drivers and operators that he would raise their concerns with the Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB). “I will deal with the LTFRB because this modernization program has been running for ages, and its implementation cannot be completed because there are […]...
